sources.entry: Flexisip - Complete, modular and scalable SIP server, includes a push gateway, to deliver SIP incoming calls or text messages on mobile device platforms where push notifications are required to receive information when the app is not active in the foreground. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 C/Docker

summary.one_liner: Flexisip is a modular, scalable SIP server suite written in C++20, including a push notification gateway for delivering SIP calls and messages to mobile devices.
summary.what_it_does: Flexisip provides a SIP proxy server that routes SIP messages, plus a push notification service that delivers in-call and message notifications to mobile devices when the app is not running in the foreground. It also includes a presence server for online status and call availability, a Back-to-Back User Agent (B2BUA) server for caller identity translation, media transcoding and SIP trunking, and a RegEvent server that notifies domains of user registrations. The README says the Conference Server moved to a separate repository from version 2.6. Configuration is generated with a dump-all-default flag, and the README describes Docker, RPM/DEB packaging, and Nix build options. Several features such as Redis, SNMP, presence, B2BUA, and OpenID Connect are optional CMake switches.
use_cases: run a self-hosted SIP VoIP service
push notifications for incoming calls on mobile apps
push notifications for SIP messages when app is backgrounded
SIP trunking and caller identity translation
embedded SIP server on small hardware
notable: Push notification gateway for mobile devices where background push is required
Modular suite: proxy, presence, B2BUA, and RegEvent servers can be enabled or disabled at build time
Powers the free linphone.org SIP service since 2011, per the README
Dual licensed: AGPLv3 or proprietary license from Belledonne Communications
Supports embedded deployment on smaller hardware
caveats: Conference Server is no longer in this repository from Flexisip 2.6 and is packaged separately
GCC 13 or newer or Clang 19 or newer is required; Debian 12 supports only Clang
Several dependencies are optional and must be enabled with CMake flags
